title: Delivery maths
story:
The pizzeria wants one place for all its delivery maths, so the till, the drivers' app and the manager's screen can all share it. Build it as a ModuleScript full of small, focused functions, then prove it works by using it from a Script.

The checker calls every function with lots of inputs, including awkward ones.
create: A ModuleScript named `DeliveryMath` inside `Test05`, returning a table of functions.

requirements.text: A ModuleScript named `DeliveryMath` and a Script named `Shift`.
`DeliveryMath` returns a table with the functions `deliveryFee`, `isLate`, `split` and `orderTotal`.
`deliveryFee(distance)` returns 3 for a distance of 2 or less. Beyond that, it adds 2 for every unit of distance over 2, so a distance of 5 costs 9.
`isLate(promisedMinutes, actualMinutes)` returns exactly `true` when the actual time is more than the promised time, otherwise exactly `false`.

`split(total, people)` returns two values: how many each person gets (whole numbers only) and how many are left over. If `people` is 0 or less, it returns `0` and the whole `total` instead of erroring.
`orderTotal(...)` takes any number of prices and returns their sum, or 0 when given none.
`Shift` requires `DeliveryMath` and prints `Fee: 9` by calling `deliveryFee` with a distance of 5.

hints: Start from the module template: a table at the top, functions added to it, and the table returned at the bottom.
For split, deal with the bad case first and return early, then use the two division operators that give whole parts and remainders.
orderTotal needs the three dots as its parameter. Count them with select and add each one up in a loop.

static.fail: Create a ModuleScript named `DeliveryMath` inside the `Test05` folder.
Create a Script named `Shift` inside the `Test05` folder.
orderTotal should take its prices with three dots, so it works with any number of them.
Shift should require the DeliveryMath module.

check:
local base = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test05."
local M, info = Course.load(base .. "DeliveryMath")
local isTable = type(M) == "table"
Course.check("r2", isTable, "DeliveryMath should return a table of functions, but it returned " .. Course.show(M) .. (if info.error then " (" .. info.error .. ")" else ""))
if isTable then
	for _, name in { "deliveryFee", "isLate", "split", "orderTotal" } do
		Course.check("r2", type(M[name]) == "function", "DeliveryMath." .. name .. " should be a function, but it's " .. Course.show(M[name]) .. ". Check the spelling and capitals.")
	end
end

local function callAll(id, name, cases, compare)
	if not isTable or type(M[name]) ~= "function" then
		Course.fail(id, "Not checked: DeliveryMath." .. name .. " is missing.")
		return
	end
	for _, case in cases do
		local args, wanted = case[1], case[2]
		local results = table.pack(Course.call(M[name], table.unpack(args)))
		local label = name .. "(" .. table.concat((function()
			local shown = {}
			for i = 1, #args do shown[i] = Course.show(args[i]) end
			return shown
		end)(), ", ") .. ")"
		if not results[1] then
			Course.fail(id, label .. " errored: " .. tostring(results[2]))
		else
			local got = { table.unpack(results, 2, results.n) }
			Course.check(id, compare(got, wanted), label .. " should return " .. Course.show(wanted) .. ", but returned " .. Course.show(got))
		end
	end
end

local function firstNear(got, wanted)
	return type(got[1]) == "number" and Course.near(got[1], wanted[1])
end
local function exactAll(got, wanted)
	if #got ~= #wanted then return false end
	for i = 1, #wanted do
		if got[i] ~= wanted[i] then return false end
	end
	return true
end

callAll("r3", "deliveryFee", { { { 0 }, { 3 } }, { { 1 }, { 3 } }, { { 2 }, { 3 } }, { { 3 }, { 5 } }, { { 5 }, { 9 } }, { { 10 }, { 19 } } }, firstNear)
callAll("r4", "isLate", { { { 30, 31 }, { true } }, { { 30, 30 }, { false } }, { { 30, 10 }, { false } }, { { 0, 1 }, { true } } }, exactAll)
callAll("r5", "split", { { { 17, 5 }, { 3, 2 } }, { { 20, 4 }, { 5, 0 } }, { { 3, 10 }, { 0, 3 } }, { { 7, 0 }, { 0, 7 } }, { { 9, -2 }, { 0, 9 } } }, exactAll)
callAll("r6", "orderTotal", { { {}, { 0 } }, { { 12 }, { 12 } }, { { 10, 12.5, 8 }, { 30.5 } }, { { 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 }, { 15 } } }, firstNear)

local run = Course.run(base .. "Shift")
Course.check("r7", run.ok, "Shift errored: " .. tostring(run.error))
Course.check("r7", table.find(run.prints, "Fee: 9") ~= nil, "Shift should print `Fee: 9`, the fee for a distance of 5, worked out by calling DeliveryMath. It printed " .. Course.show(run.prints))
steps: In the `DeliveryMath` tab, make a table, add four functions to it (written as the table's name, a dot, then the function name), and `return` the table on the last line.
`deliveryFee(distance)`: a distance of 2 or less costs 3. Further than that costs 3 plus 2 for every unit past 2. So `deliveryFee(2)` gives `3`, and `deliveryFee(5)` gives `3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 9`.
`isLate(promisedMinutes, actualMinutes)`: returns `true` if actual is more than promised, otherwise `false`. So `isLate(30, 31)` gives `true`, and `isLate(30, 30)` gives `false`.
`split(total, people)`: returns two numbers, how many each person gets (whole numbers) and how many are left over. So `split(17, 5)` gives `3, 2`. If people is 0 or less, return `0, total` instead.
`orderTotal(...)`: takes any number of prices and returns their sum. So `orderTotal(10, 12.5, 8)` gives `30.5`, and `orderTotal()` gives `0`.
In the `Shift` tab, require the module with `require(script.Parent.DeliveryMath)`, then print `Fee: ` followed by the fee for a distance of 5.
example:
Running the Shift tab prints:
Fee: 9
